title: Verdict stamp's 'parseable' field is write-only: produced and test-pinned, but no production code ever reads it
location: tenant_scorer/callbacks/compliance_enforcement.py:164; guard consumes only passed/violation_count at boundary_compliance_remediation.py:334-338 and final_compliance_remediation.py:280-284
detail: Grep confirms no get("parseable") anywhere in tenant_scorer/; both finalize guards consume only passed/violation_count/judge_kind and hardcode "review_parseable": False in the log extra. The field is dead state on a temp slot, pinned only by the W1 test assertions.
recommended_fix: Drop 'parseable' from the stamp (and its test assertions), or have the guards log the stamp's parseable value instead of the hardcoded False.

title: r1 note (temp verdict-stamp slot never cleared) still present since round 1 — r2 added no pop
detail: r1 note #2 unchanged by the r2 delta: agent.py finally blocks pop only STATE_COMPLIANCE_JUDGE_META; STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT is never cleared, so invocation-locality rests entirely on the temp: prefix trim (safe for Database/Vertex, leaky for a reused InMemory session).
recommended_fix: Pop STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT in the same finally blocks that pop STATE_COMPLIANCE_JUDGE_META, for symmetry and explicit invocation-locality.

title: r1 note (STATE_PIPELINE_ERROR written via plain session dict bypasses the node event-delta) still present since round 1
detail: r1 note #1 unchanged: finalize receives the live ctx.session.state dict, so the error write is not recorded in the node's event_actions.state_delta for session rewind/replay. Mitigated by rerun_on_resume=True (node re-runs and re-sets the error); single-invocation behavior is correct.
recommended_fix: Optional: also set the flag on ctx.state so it lands in the node delta, or document that STATE_PIPELINE_ERROR is intentionally invocation-local.

title: r1 note (stringly-typed judge_kind with implicit else) still present since round 1 — r2 call sites reuse the same literals
detail: r1 note #4 unchanged: _judge_kind's implicit else maps any unknown review key to 'final', and the guards pass the same hand-typed string literals. A typo in either would silently disable one gate's cross-check (fail-closed direction — safe but silent). Narrow: only two keys exist today.
recommended_fix: Optional: derive judge_kind from a shared constant or map with an explicit error for unknown keys, so producer and consumer cannot drift.

detail: r1 note #5 unchanged: the boundary gate scrubs via ctx.state while the review read now uses ctx.session.state — the same view divergence the fix routes around. Out of scope for this PR (dirty path only, passes in production); the r2 delta deliberately did not touch it.
